summary: Customer session export + compliance SOP for third-party audit request
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Retail, enterprise) has requested a targeted export of session logs and associated request/response payloads for a pending third-party security audit. They specifically asked for sessions touching a set of customer IDs and date range (2026-02-20 through 2026-03-05).

Impact:
Potential exposure of customer-identifying fields if redaction is incomplete. Request requires coordination across SRE (log extraction), Security (KMS & key access), and Legal/Compliance (contract & audit scope). Time-sensitive due to audit window; customer flagged as enterprise SLA.

Requested deliverables:
- Extract full request+response records for session IDs provided by customer or for the specified date range and customer IDs.
- Provide redaction metadata and confirmation of PII removal (or fields retained with justification).
- Delivery method: secure SFTP to customer-managed location OR temporary signed URL with strict expiry; Legal prefers SFTP to their auditor account.
- Audit trail: who accessed, query filters used, and KMS key IDs used to decrypt artifacts.

Why this is tricky:
- Production logs live in an encrypted S3 path with KMS envelope encryption and are indexed by a streaming pipeline; naive extraction risks including KV cache or non-redacted traces.
- Previous tickets (INT-4312, INT-5789) flagged gaps in how partial redaction was documented. We must avoid ad-hoc manual copies without an auditable workflow.
request_details: Customer-specified scope: customer_ids: [ACME-92, ACME-239], date_range: 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-05, include request and model response payloads, include request metadata (IP, timestamp, route). Delivery: SFTP to auditor@acme-audit.example.com; retention: 30 days; encryption: at-rest AES-256; requester: Acme legal - contact: sarah.liu@acme.com
environment_notes: Logs are stored in s3://redwood-prod-logs/session-archive/ and indexed in ES cluster logging-prod-3. Extraction pipeline must use the authorized read role 'log-extract-audit' and an extraction job should run from the support-runner namespace to ensure RBAC and egress controls. KMS key: projects/redwood/cryptoKeys/prod-logs-kms (access control required).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Confirm exact session identifiers or confirm customer IDs and date range.
2) Open a temporary gated extraction job in staging extraction-runner to validate query filters (use sample data).
3) Run extraction against production with logging enabled and 'dry-run' flag first to list objects that would be exported.
4) Apply redaction toolchain (redact-utils v1.3) to extracted payloads and produce an audit manifest listing redaction rationale for each field.
5) Coordinate with Security to provision SFTP credentials to auditor account and provide single-use passphrase stored in Vault.

comments: Nina Morales (Support) - 2026-03-10: Created ticket after intake call with Acme. They supplied an initial CSV of session IDs; asking for ETA and whether PII redaction can be certified.

Ethan Brooks (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Will validate KMS access and run a non-destructive dry-run. Noted that 'log-extract-audit' role currently lacks decrypt permission for prod-logs-kms. Raising to Security to request temporary grant.

Dara Chen (Security) - 2026-03-11: We can approve a scoped grant but require Legal sign-off on auditor identity and a short-term IAM binding. Need Confluence page signed: Compliance/Third-Party-Audit-Checklist.
Liam Patel (Legal) - 2026-03-11: Requested confirmation that sensitive fields (credit_card, ssn, full_email) will be redacted. Also asked for copy of auditor NDA; customer to provide.
Ethan Brooks (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Performed dry-run; found 1,236 matching objects totaling ~8.3GB. Dry-run manifest attached to ticket (link: s3://support-temp/INT-8591/dryrun-manifest.json).
investigation_notes: Dry-run output: 1,236 objects; several payloads include 'user_email' and 'billing_account_id' fields that must be redacted.

KMS policy: prod-logs-kms currently allows decryption for roles: 'log-reader', 'support-ops'; 'log-extract-audit' missing decrypt. Proposal: temporary policy grant scoped to extraction job with automatic revocation after 72 hours.
Redaction tooling: redact-utils v1.3 flags ambiguous fields named 'acc' or 'acctId' - need mapping to canonical schema to avoid misses.

SRE recommends: export pipeline produce two outputs: (1) raw encrypted bundle for internal audit under stricter controls, (2) redacted bundle for customer/auditor. Keep manifest linking originals to redacted artefacts in Vault-only access.
next_steps: 1) Legal to confirm auditor identity and NDA (owner: Liam Patel).
2) Security to approve temporary KMS decrypt grant and create short-lived IAM binding (owner: Dara Chen).
3) SRE to run extraction with dry-run approved filters and produce redacted bundle using redact-utils; produce audit manifest (owner: Ethan Brooks).
4) Support to coordinate delivery and update customer with ETA once all approvals are in place (owner: Nina Morales).
resolution: Pending approvals: legal and security sign-offs required before extraction. No delivery until redaction and audit manifest validated.
follow_up_actions: Create a reusable runbook for targeted log exports that standardizes dry-run, redaction, and delivery steps (owner: SRE).
Add automated KMS grant playbook for time-limited decrypt access to reduce manual overhead (owner: Security).
